text:
morgan: FYI seeing sporadic 401s from Rust streaming client (tokio+hyper) in staging when using OIDC token-exchange impersonation. Happens after ~15-20m idle; reconnects sometimes succeed, sometimes fail.

jai: do you have the failure body? is it 'invalid_audience' or generic 401?

morgan: server returns 401 with body: "error: invalid_audience, expected aud=redwood-inference:service:ingest got aud=projects/PROJ-B". Token-exchange initial jwt used aud=projects/PROJ-B, but final access_token aud is the service name.

sasha: sounds like connection resumed with an old token or routing relies on aud at connection time. Are you reusing the same long-lived HTTP2 stream without re-auth?

morgan: yes we reuse the same HTTP2 stream. we refresh token only when expiry < 30s. idle period >15m seems to trigger mismatch after some routing update.

oliver: I've seen this. If the control plane changes routing rules, an existing stream may be re-evaluated and backend verifies aud against route. Two mitigations: 1) refresh token before resuming after idle, 2) annotate stream with explicit x-service-aud header derived from the final access_token.

jai: also ensure your token-exchange returns the 'aud' claim consistently. If impersonation chain returns a different subject/principal, the aud might change. Always derive routing header from the access_token you *actually* received.

morgan: practical change plan: lower refresh threshold to 10m, force re-eval on resume, and log token fingerprint per connection. any code pointers for Rust?

sasha: simple pattern:

```rust
// before resuming a stream
if last_auth.elapsed() > Duration::from_secs(600) {
  let t = auth.refresh().await?; // get fresh access_token
  conn.set_header("authorization", format!("Bearer {}", t.token));
  conn.set_header("x-aud", t.aud.clone());
}
```

oliver: add exponential backoff with jitter for 401 so you don't hammer token-exchange. on first 401, force refresh once, then backoff.

morgan: good call. also: should we keep aud as the audience in the initial JWT we send to token-exchange, or request aud=final_service every time?

jai: request aud=final_service. The token-exchange can return a different principal; your client should not assume aud propagation. Request target audit explicitly.

ci-bot: canary: rust-client patch applied to staging — auth-resume-refresh=600s, added token-fingerprint logs. build #b720 passed :white_check_mark:

morgan: thanks. I'll open PR for the lower threshold + 401 refresh and tag @oliver for review. test plan: 1) simulate idle 30m 2) change route on control plane 3) verify no persistent 401 loops 4) check metrics: last_aud_per_conn and token_fingerprint.

oliver: lgtm. ping when PR ready and include unit test for reauth-on-resume.

morgan: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
